checks: The server MUST run the FIPS 203 section 7.2 encapsulation key check on the client's encapsulation key and abort with an illegal_parameter alert if it fails (RFC 10024 section 4.2).
The client MUST check that the ciphertext length matches the selected group and abort with an illegal_parameter alert if it fails (RFC 10024 section 4.2).
If ML-KEM decapsulation fails for any other reason, the connection MUST be aborted with an internal_error alert (RFC 10024 section 4.2).
Both sides MUST process the ECDHE part as described in RFC 9846 section 4.3.8.2, including all validity checks, and abort with an illegal_parameter alert if it fails (RFC 10024 section 4.2).

Both sides MUST calculate the ECDHE part of the shared secret as described in RFC 9846 section 7.4.2, including the all-zero shared secret check for X25519, and abort with an illegal_parameter alert if it fails (RFC 10024 section 4.3).
All groups use fixed-length public keys, ciphertexts, and shared secrets (RFC 10024 section 6).
source: RFC 10024, Post-Quantum Traditional (PQ/T) Hybrid Key Agreement Mechanisms for TLS 1.3, Kwiatkowski, Kampanakis, Westerbaan and Stebila, August 2026. Harvested 2026-11-05 from the RFC text at rfc-editor.org (sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 6 and 7.1-7.4). RFC 10024 publishes no test vectors and no worked examples: what it fixes is the group geometry below, the concatenation orders, the code points, and the checks listed. The byte-level vectors it relies on come from FIPS 203 (the ACVP set in mlkem768_acvp.json) and RFC 7748 (transcribed in runner/tests/test_dtls.py and runner/tools/hybrid_fuzz.py).
